verdict.rationale: a-Shell's own `pickFolder` command opens directories inside other apps' sandboxes. Users can then work on those files, for example running Python or TeX there, and the folders are bookmarked for later return. Nothing in the pack shows repository-specific workflows, such as git operations on repos stored in another app's sandbox. missing for 10: evidence of working with repositories (e.g., git clone/commit/push) in other apps' sandboxes, independent or hands-on corroboration of pickFolder behavior and its limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can access and work with files and repositories from other apps' sandboxes on my device

citations.quote: a-Shell uses iOS 13 ability to access directories in other Apps sandbox. Type `pickFolder` to access a directory inside another App.
Once you have selected a directory, you can do pretty much anything you want here
You can open directories in other app sandbox with pickFolder and run TeX or Python there.
All the directories you access with `pickFolder` are bookmarked, so you can return to them later without `pickFolder`.
